title: Republic of Uryankhay
capsule: The Uryankhay (Tuvan) Republic was a nominally independent polity proclaimed in the Tuva basin following the Xinhai Revolution of 1911, when Qing China's collapse prompted local Tuvan nobles to seek separation from both China and the newly independent Outer Mongolia. The new state was driven by a faction of khural nobles who preferred Russian imperial protection; Tsar Nicholas II despatched a military detachment in 1912 and formalised Russian authority on 14 April 1914, converting the republic into the protectorate of Uryankhay Krai under Russian administration. The region passed through further political transformations—briefly reverting to Chinese influence, then becoming the Tuvan People's Republic in 1921 before annexation into the Soviet Union as Tuva Oblast in 1944.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Uryankhay Republic's territorial extent is broadly defined by the Tuva basin geography, but formal administrative demarcation from Outer Mongolia and China during 1911–1914 was contested and imprecise.
